_: Street types and the rules that name them (tools/mapworld/streets/rules.ts, planning/workstreams/streets.md). A type is a name and a default section. The rules are read in order: the first whose `when` holds and which names a `type` gives the stretch its type; then every rule whose `when` holds and which has `set` changes its section's fields, side by side, in order. A city's rules.json `streets` lays its own over these: its types by name, its rules first, one with a shared rule's id in that rule's place. Widths are metres; a pair [least, most] is chosen between by the stretch's seed.

fields.kerb: raised, flush (no kerb: the asphalt meets its verge level) or worn (raised and broken down)
fields.verge: none, planted (a tidy strip of lawn), grass (rough grass), dirt, paved or gravel: between the kerb and the walk, or a median's side
fields.vergeWidth: metres from the kerb to the walk
fields.walk: none, walk (of walkWidth) or full (from the verge to the building line, at least the least of walkWidth and at most its most)
fields.walkAt: kerb (the verge's width as the section says) or drawn (the walk where the data draws one on that side, the verge between)
fields.median: none, planted, paved or barrier: the ground between a pair of one-way carriageways, from each kerb to the middle
fields.parking: none, one or both: kerbside parking lanes (reported; the carriageway is still the data's width)
fields.wear: 0 to 1, how worn (reported; the lane wear still reads the road's class)

highway.about: Motorways and trunk roads: no kerb, rough shoulders, no walk, a barrier between the carriageways.

boulevard.about: A pair of one-way carriageways with a planted median, walks at the kerb outside.

downtown.about: A city centre's street: kerb, no verge, the walk from the kerb to the building line.

main-street.about: A shopping street out of the centre: kerb, no verge, a wide walk.

residential-tidy.about: A kept street of houses: kerb, a planted verge, a walk behind it (where the data draws one, there).

residential-rough.about: A poor or neglected street of houses: a worn kerb, rough grass and dirt, a narrow walk.

alley.about: A service lane, an alley, a driveway: no kerb, its asphalt crumbling into what is beside it, no walk.

industrial.about: A street of works and yards: no kerb, a gravel verge, no walk.
